<PubmedArticle><MedlineCitation Status="MEDLINE" Owner="NLM" IndexingMethod="Manual"><PMID Version="1">2849457</PMID><DateCompleted><Year>1989</Year><Month>02</Month><Day>02</Day></DateCompleted><DateRevised><Year>2019</Year><Month>08</Month><Day>24</Day></DateRevised><Article PubModel="Print"><Journal><ISSN IssnType="Print">0166-4328</ISSN><JournalIssue CitedMedium="Print"><Volume>31</Volume><Issue>2</Issue><PubDate><Year>1988</Year><Month>Dec</Month><Day>01</Day></PubDate></JournalIssue><Title>Behavioural brain research</Title><ISOAbbreviation>Behav Brain Res</ISOAbbreviation></Journal><ArticleTitle>Delayed response deficit in monkeys by locally disturbed prefrontal neuronal activity by bicuculline.</ArticleTitle><Pagination><StartPage>193</StartPage><EndPage>198</EndPage><MedlinePgn>193-8</MedlinePgn></Pagination><Abstract><AbstractText>Effects of local injection of a gamma-aminobutyric acid antagonist, bicuculline (10-30 micrograms dissolved in saline) in the principal prefrontal cortex on the delayed response task were investigated in two monkeys. On a visual Go signal, the monkeys rotated a handle to the left or to the right (Go period) according to a visual cue (left or right; 1 s) presented 4 s earlier. Bicuculline induced bursting activity at the injected site 1-2 min after the injection and 5 min later the burst activity spread to nearby cortical areas (less than 4 mm diameter). Within 5 min after injection, the monkeys showed errors in Go periods, rotating the handle to the contralateral zone, regardless of the cue side. This tendency continued for 30-40 min and returned to the control level. Electromyographic recordings of forearm muscles did not show any changes. The effect was observed when the drug was injected into a circumscribed area of the bottom of the mid-principalis region. It appears that disturbed neuronal activity in a small group of cortical columns induces performance errors of specific direction of the delayed response.</AbstractText></Abstract><AuthorList
